summary: Cockpit is a control center for software written with AI agents: it shows the project's own description (features and diagrams kept in .cockpit/) live, lights up what an agent is editing, and puts files, git, terminals and the agent chat beside it. A Node server per project (with a Svelte page and a GTK desktop shell around it) indexes the code, runs Claude Code through the Agent SDK and records each turn.

features.name: Live map of diagrams
features.description: Agent-written diagrams (loop, pipeline, dataflow, zones) drawn from .cockpit/, explained on hover and in a card over the map when a box is clicked, zoomable down to the code of a box, with boxes of uncommitted or in-progress code marked. Boxes can be dragged anywhere (with Shift they snap into line with other boxes, guides shown) or nudged with the arrow keys, and stay where you put them.

features.name: Files and git
features.description: File tree and editor (CodeMirror, vim keys, language servers) showing uncommitted changes in place, and a git tab with the branch, its PR/MR, status and a commit graph; a project tab beside them lists features, tests, out-of-date links and guardrails.

features.name: Agent chat
features.description: Runs Claude Code through the Agent SDK on the user's login: sessions, several agents working at once (one per conversation, switching leaves the others running, the title shows how many work or wait for you), a model menu (opus by default), messages typed while it works, images pasted or dropped into the message, one send/stop button, Allow/Deny cards, context and plan-limit meters, and a self-check that sends the agent back when .cockpit/ or a guardrail no longer holds.

features.name: Turns and live lighting
features.description: Every agent request is a turn recorded with before/after snapshots in cockpit's own git store; the files it touches light up the map as it works. Claude Code sessions outside cockpit are recorded through hooks.

features.name: Terminals
features.description: Real shells in the project with command marks, readable by the agent, plus a Ctrl+K line that turns words into a command without running it.

features.name: Review mode
features.description: Check out a merge request or two branches and see changed boxes, files and git lists against the point where the branch left its target. The merge request's discussions (glab/gh) show under their lines in the editor and in the git tab, and the agent reads them through its review_threads tool.

features.name: Guardrails
features.description: Checks (commands) and rules (with why and enforcement layer) in .cockpit/guardrails.json, run at the end of a turn that edited files; the agent is sent back for checks it broke. They are the project's own shell commands, so none run until you trust them as they are (again after a pull or branch changes them; the chat agent's own edits are trusted).

features.name: Private descriptions and workspaces
features.description: A project's .cockpit/ can be kept out of its repo, per branch, and synced between machines through a private repo; a workspace (a folder in cockpit's settings with a workspace.json; listed, created and extended from the project menu) opens all its projects in one window, like an editor's multi-root workspace, while opening one of its projects opens just that one. The workspace's host is none of its projects: it runs a server per project, and the window shows every project's files (a root folder each), git (a section each), quick open, search and diagrams (the map's breadcrumb and list pick the project).
features.note: Terminals and the chat are still one project's (the page's server); the chat agent asks before editing another project

features.name: Code index (Rust, C/C++, Zig, TypeScript)
features.description: Builds the modules and items that .cockpit/ links name: rust-analyzer or scip-clang SCIP indexes, or cockpit's own scanners for Zig and TypeScript/JavaScript (with a Rust crate beside a TypeScript project added in). The modules and check-arch commands print and check against it.
features.note: The TypeScript scanner doesn't follow tsconfig path aliases, and a quote in JSX text can confuse it for the rest of that file.

features.name: Desktop app
features.description: A GTK 4 / libadwaita window (WebKitGTK) that starts one server per project on a free port, switches projects in place, follows the desktop's accent and window buttons, and stops the servers when closed. Each server only lets in the page opened with its token (a random one per server from the app, or the link `npm run serve` prints), and refuses other host names for 127.0.0.1.
